title: GE Aerospace Investing $225M to Modernize Research Center
summary: Securing NY's role at the forefront of aerospace innovation, State of New York commits an additional $8.4M to support transformational projectNISKAYUNA, N.Y. — September 21, 2026 —
body_markdown:
*Securing NY's role at the forefront of aerospace innovation, State of New York commits an additional $8.4M to support transformational project*


**NISKAYUNA, N.Y.** — September 21, 2026 — GE Aerospace today announced a $225 million investment to modernize the GE Aerospace Research Center in Niskayuna, NY, advancing the site's legacy as the innovation engine behind breakthroughs in aviation advancements. The State of New York has also committed $8.4 million in tax credits through Empire State Development (ESD) to the project, with Schenectady County Metroplex Development Authority contributing additional local incentives valued at $5.3 million.


Joseph Vinciquerra, general manager and senior executive director, GE Aerospace Research, said, “The future of flight is developed through rigorous scientific and technical pursuit spanning decades. We are ready to turn this investment into breakthroughs that will define the next era of aviation. We are grateful to our state and regional partners for their support and continued commitment to New York's role in our nation’s pursuit of aerospace advancement.”


"New York State has a bold legacy of innovation, built on the shoulders of big ideas and big investments by globally renowned companies like GE Aerospace. We want to ensure that the next generation of technological discoveries happens here, and today's announcement demonstrates that our legacy is only getting stronger,” said Governor Kathy Hochul. “Working together with GE Aerospace, we are bringing the jobs and developments of tomorrow to the Capital Region today."


For more than 75 years, the GE Aerospace Research Center has served as a premier technology development hub. Today, it is the engine powering GE Aerospace's next generation breakthroughs across AI, autonomy, robotics, advanced materials, future manufacturing, hypersonic propulsion, and hybrid electric flight.


The combined investments will:


- **Modernize the Niskayuna site** to strengthen GE Aerospace's research capacity, with approximately two-thirds going toward infrastructure improvements and the remainder dedicated to advanced research equipment and technology.
- **Create 75 new full-time, high-paying jobs** over five years, generate short-term construction employment, and safeguard the future of the scientists, engineers, researchers, and skilled laborers who already call Niskayuna home. The new positions will include a mix of research and engineering roles and trade positions.
- **Support execution of advanced technology projects** with partners in both academia and the federal sector, particularly Department of Energy and Department of War projects funded through Congressional appropriations.


GE Aerospace expects to begin site improvement projects immediately, and research operations at Niskayuna will continue with minimal disruption throughout construction.


Senator Chuck Schumer said, “GE Aerospace’s new $225 million investment in Niskayuna, along with 75 high-skilled, good-paying jobs, shows the sky is the limit for our top-notch workforce. I have long supported the company’s growth in Upstate New York and am thrilled that the workforce expansion of GE Aerospace Research in Niskayuna and upgrades to the campus are on their way to the Capital Region. Investments like this are key to ensuring that cutting-edge aerospace technology research is happening at home in places like Schenectady County. I will keep fighting to support investments in the equipment we need to strengthen New York’s research and manufacturing leadership.”


Congressman Paul D. Tonko, NY-20, said, “Our Capital Region has long served as a global hub for technology and innovation, and GE Aerospace has played a key role in that proud tradition for many, many years. Today’s announcement adds a new chapter to that history. This investment of $225 million to modernize and upgrade the GE Aerospace Research Center in Niskayuna will allow GE Aerospace to shape the future of aviation right here in our Capital Region, bringing good-paying jobs and economic development that will benefit all who call our region home. I’m thrilled to celebrate this historic step forward, and I’m eager to see the impact it will have not only here in Niskayuna, but across the entire aerospace industry.”


Chair of the Schenectady County Legislature Gary Hughes said, “This is a fantastic commitment by GE Aerospace towards the future of flight at the company’s research center. It will boost the leading-edge jet engine R&D work done in Niskayuna that is critical to the future of both military and commercial aviation. Our county economic development team worked with Governor Hochul and Empire State Development for more than a year to win this investment and we thank GE Aerospace for this great news that will boost our local economy.”


**About GE Aerospace Research**
GE Aerospace Research develops and advances critical technologies that support GE Aerospace’s enterprise priorities and help define the future of flight. Working closely with GE Aerospace businesses and external collaborators, Research translates innovation into practical application in areas such as AI, autonomy, robotics, advanced materials, future manufacturing, and hybrid electric and electric power — creating clear customer value and strengthening long-term competitive advantage.


**About GE Aerospace**
GE Aerospace is a global aerospace propulsion, services, and systems leader with an installed base of approximately 50,000 commercial and 30,000 military aircraft engines. With a global team of approximately 57,000 employees building on more than a century of innovation and learning, GE Aerospace is committed to inventing the future of flight, lifting people up, and bringing them home safely. Learn more about how GE Aerospace and its partners are defining flight for today, tomorrow, and the future at www.geaerospace.com.


**About Empire State Development**


Empire State Development is New York's chief economic development agency, and promotes business growth, job creation, and greater economic opportunity throughout the state. With offices in each of the state's 10 regions, ESD oversees the Regional Economic Development Councils, supports broadband equity through the ConnectALL office, and is growing the workforce of tomorrow through the Office of Strategic Workforce Development. The agency engages with emerging and next generation industries like clean energy and semiconductor manufacturing looking to grow in New York State, operates a network of assistance centers to help small businesses grow and succeed, and promotes the state's world class tourism destinations through[I LOVE NY](http://www.iloveny.com/) .
